acceptance.description: How this task will be judged done, in a form someone can check: a command and its expected output, or the exact steps and result. Required: a task without it can only be judged by hand, after integration, which is where 2026-10-05's most expensive rework happened.

assigned_worker_id.description: The Agent this row is handed to. Required: coordination.plan sends one task.assigned message per row to this Agent and wakes it.

cross_module.description: Declares that this task shares an interface with another module. Declaring it makes required_contract_ids mandatory in the same row: the most expensive semantic conflict on 2026-10-05 (a reader calling /requests while the backend served /api/applications) overlapped no files at all, so a contract enforced only on file overlap cannot catch it.

dependencies.description: Task ids this row waits for (blocks edges). The dependency gate only accepts a dependency whose status is completed.

execution_scope.description: Same shape as task.create: {"roots": [...]} or {"resources": [...]}. Empty means the task claims no path.

parent_task_id.description: Navigation only: this does not make the parent wait for the child.

required_contract_ids.description: Accepted contract ids this row depends on -- the proposal_id/contract_id contract.propose returned, never a label of your own.

supersedes_task_id.description: The task this one replaces. The named task leaves the claim queue and keeps a link to its replacement, so 'we changed our minds' stays readable instead of looking like unfinished work.

task_objective.description: What this task must produce. This is the row's objective, not the plan's top-level objective.

workspace.description: A workspace.select payload for this row (task_id is filled in). Given it, the plan selects the policy in the same call instead of leaving it to begin.
